key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain boundaries increases cohesion, with gains depending on the alloying element and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Validated atomistic cohesion predictions could supply inputs for continuum fracture models of multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic foundation models against DFT, then use a validated model to sample binary and ternary alloy configurations.
evidence_signal: One tested ML interatomic potential achieved quantitative agreement with DFT for work of separation and maximum traction, enabling finer concentration sampling.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations are needed.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
